# Introduction
The University of Wisconsin-Madison book club is curious whether cover color can reliably distinguish one genre from another. The club asked students in Data Science in Human Behavior to investigate.

# Literacture Review
Several earlier studies have applied machine learning to predict book characteristics from one observable input, which provides a foundation for the present analysis.  [@vayadande2024book]

# Method
```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import seaborn as sns

from scipy import stats
from scipy.stats import chi2_contingency

domain = 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/'
path = 'adamrossnelson/confident/refs/heads/main/data/'
file = 'confident_fictional_books.csv'

books = pd.read_csv(domain + path + file)
```


Our null hypothesis is that book cover color does not predict the book's genre while the alternate hypothesis is that book cover color does 
predict the book's genre and we study this question with data from `{python} f"{books.shape[0]}"` books where we know the book's genre and 
the book's cover color such that we can conduct a chi2 test to see if these two varaibles are either independent or dependent 

(as it turns out our chi2 test will involve a

` {python} f"{books['book_genre'].nunique()}" ` x

` {python} f"{books['book_color'].nunique()}" ` test ) 

# Results
```{python}
#Conduct he chi2 with chi2_contingency by passing the observed
x2, pval, degf, _  = chi2_contingency (
  pd.crosstab(
    books['book_genre'],
    books['book_color']
  )
)
```

Chi2 Stat: `{python} f"{x2: .3f}"` 

Pvalue: `{python} f"{pval: .3f}"` 

Degrees of Freedom: `{python} f"{degf}"`

With a chi-square statistic of 1.992 on 25 degrees of freedom and a p-value of 1.000, we fail to reject the null hypothesis, so there is no evidence that book cover color is associated with a book's genre.

# Discussion
Our results suggest that cover color alone is not a useful way to separate books by genre, so the book club would be better off relying on other features such as title, description, or cover imagery.

"It is a sad day for the UW-Madison book club members, the DSHB students thought they could deliver a BIG WIN for the book club members and book addicionados world-wide; the search for a reproducible method that will predict book genre carries on!"
